pages.transcription:
Wyndham Motel                                Sunday evening, May 18th, 41

Dear Hanna & Manfred, I have just returned from Croton
and have nothing but the very best and satisfactory to
tell you about Eva. She feels fine, looks very well, loves
Amity Hall and the country round it (which
with its rolling hills has really some resemblance with Bath).
Yesterday Mr. Kiefer visited her and they went for a drive
and walk. I suppose he will write you about his impressions
and I am confident that his report will contribute further
to reassure you about her surroundings. Today we went
for a visit to Fueloep-Miller's, our friends - I believe you
have met them in Hallam Street - who are in Croton over
the summer with a 3 months old baby whom Eva admired
very much and whom she is invited to visit. As they are
on best terms with Schaeffer's I suppose that will be easy.
If Eva's letter from today should be a little shorter
than usual, you must blame it on me because I left
an hour later than usual. Both Eva and I had a nice
letter from Miss Baker, and she promised to call me up when
she comes to New York. - Salmon's are silent and in spite of
various letters not a line is to be got out of them. There
is nothing to be done - and I don't think it is important.
They mean well - when they happen to think of Eva - but
they are unreliable and have no manners. And as Eva
is now in very good hands and we do not intend to
leave the country we do not need them. - Eva will have
written you that she spent the last weekend with a friend
in Croton. Mrs. Sh told me that the girl and her parents
are extremely nice and Eva enjoyed it. She brought some
photos and I enclose a small one. - Some other visitors to
Amity Hall took me back to New York and I felt quite
grown-up, discussing the children and their various
little problems, summer holidays, etc. - I hope you have
at last finished with the dentist. You are to be much more
pitied than I. I am much better and the twice-weekly visit
to the doctor means no more than a few injections - three at
one time, a "mezihe", as the doctor calls it.

[Randnotiz links:] Did Manfred brother it [?] to see mother? - And what was, if any, your kind regard and bad love [?]
